records.literal_gloss: For the director, on the gittith. Of [the] sons of Korah. A psalm.

en.L: For the director: on the gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
en.B: For the music director. On the gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
en.R: For the leader of the music. Set to "the Gittith". By the family of Korah. A song.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : sur la guittith. Des fils de Coré. Un psaume.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Sur la guittith. Des fils de Coré. Un psaume.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. Sur l’air de « la Guittith ». De la famille de Coré. Un chant.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: juu ya gitithi. Ya wana wa Kora. Zaburi.
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Kwa gitithi. Ya wana wa Kora. Zaburi.
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Kwa mtindo wa "Gitithi". Ya ukoo wa Kora. Wimbo.

es.L: Al director del coro: sobre el gitit. De los hijos de Coré. Salmo.
es.B: Al director del coro. Sobre el gitit. De los hijos de Coré. Salmo.
es.R: Para el director de la música. Con la música de «el gitit». De la familia de Coré. Canto.

vi.L: Cho người chỉ huy [ban nhạc]: theo ghít-tít. Của con cháu Cô-ra. [Một] thi thiên.
vi.B: Cho nhạc trưởng. Theo ghít-tít. Thi thiên của con cháu Cô-ra.
vi.R: Cho người hướng dẫn ban nhạc. Theo điệu "Ghít-tít". Bài ca của gia đình Cô-ra.

ko.L: 지휘자를 위하여. 깃딧에 맞추어. 고라 자손의 [것]. 시.
ko.B: 음악 지휘자를 위하여. 깃딧에 맞추어. 고라 자손의 시.
ko.R: 찬양 인도자를 위해 '깃딧'에 맞추어 부르는, 고라 집안 사람들이 지은 노래.

pt.L: Para o regente: sobre a gitite. Dos filhos de Corá. Salmo.
pt.B: Para o mestre de música. Sobre a gitite. Dos filhos de Corá. Salmo.
pt.R: Para quem dirige a música. No tom da "Gitite". Da família de Corá. Uma canção.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: the gittith: an instrument or tune, perhaps from Gath
decisions.reason: The word (gittit) is found in the titles of Psalms 8, 81 and 84. It may be an instrument or tune from the city of Gath, or be linked with the word for a winepress (gat). Its sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a family of Levite singers
decisions.reason: The descendants of Korah, a Levite (Numbers 26:11), served as gatekeepers and singers at the temple (1 Chronicles 9:19; 2 Chronicles 20:19). Eleven psalms carry their name (42-49, 84-85, 87-88). "Of" may mean the psalm belongs to their collection or was written by one of them.

decisions.choice: "Au chef de chœur" (Literal, Balanced) and "Pour le chef des musiciens" (Readable); "un psaume" (Literal, Balanced), "un chant" (Readable), for Psalms 84-104
decisions.reason: As set for the whole of Psalms in French, so that the titles read alike in every part of the book. The gittith keeps its Hebrew name in French spelling ("guittith"), since its sense is unknown (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya" (L, B) and "Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji" (R) for the director; "zaburi" (L, B) and "wimbo" (R) for a psalm, through Psalms 84-104
alternatives: "Kwa mkuu wa waimbaji" at every level
decisions.reason: The title names the leader of the temple music; "kwaya" is the everyday word for a choir, and Readable says plainly that he led the singers. "Zaburi" is the Swahili name for a psalm; Readable calls it a song, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "gitithi", kept as a name at every level
decisions.reason: Nobody now knows what the gittith was: an instrument or tune from Gath, or something to do with a winepress. Swahili keeps the Hebrew word as a name, as the English does, rather than guess.

decisions.choice: Al director del coro (L, B); Para el director de la música (R); Salmo (L, B); Canto (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lamnatseach names the one who led the temple music, and mizmor is a song sung to music. Spanish follows the English levels: "director del coro" and "Salmo" at Literal and Balanced, "director de la música" and "Canto" at Readable. In a title Spanish leaves out the article ("Salmo", not "Un salmo"). These forms are used in all the psalm titles that follow.

decisions.choice: el gitit
alternatives: translating it as an instrument or a tune
decisions.reason: The word gittit is no longer understood (it may be an instrument or a tune from Gath). Spanish keeps it as a name, as the English does, and Readable says only that the psalm goes with it.

decisions.choice: "ghít-tít" kept as a name (L, B); "theo điệu Ghít-tít" (R)
decisions.reason: The word's sense is lost: it may be an instrument or a tune from Gath (see the meaning decision). Vietnamese keeps it as a name, as the English does, and Readable calls it a tune, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Cô-ra" (L, B); "gia đình Cô-ra" (R)
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means descendants, a family of Levite singers (see the meaning decision). "con cháu" says that; Readable says "family", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "지휘자를 위하여" (L), "음악 지휘자를 위하여" (B), "찬양 인도자를 위해" (R); "시" (L, B), "노래" (R)
decisions.reason: As the published Psalm 139:1 and the terms note, so that every psalm title reads alike; Readable says "song" as the English Readable does. This holds for the titles of Psalms 84-104.

decisions.choice: "깃딧" kept as a name; "고라 자손" (L, B), "고라 집안 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning of gittith is not known (meaning decision m3), so Korean keeps it as a name, as the English does, in the form Korean Bible readers know. Readable says "family" for the sons of Korah, as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: How beloved [are] your dwellings, YHWH of hosts!

en.B: How deeply loved is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dwelling place, \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies!
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q the place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} live is so dear to me!

fr.B: Comme elle est aimée, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} demeure, \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées !
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q j’aime tant l’endroit où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} habites !

sw.L: Jinsi yanavyopendwa makao {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi!
sw.B: Makao {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yanapendwa mno, \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi!
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q mahali unapoishi ni pa thamani sana kwangu!

es.B: ¡Cuán querido es el lugar donde {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} habitas, \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos!
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q ¡cuánto amo el lugar donde {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} vives!

vi.L: Các nơi ngự của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáng yêu dấu biết bao, \q lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân!
vi.B: Nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngự thật đáng yêu quý biết bao, \q lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân!
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q tôi yêu mến biết bao nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở!

ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, \q 주님께서 계시는 곳이 얼마나 사랑스러운지요!
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, \q 주님께서 계시는 곳이 저는 정말 좋습니다!

pt.L: Quão amadas [são] as {{deity_pronoun:tuas|Tuas}} moradas, \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos!
pt.B: Quão amáveis são as {{deity_pronoun:tuas|Tuas}} moradas, \q {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos!
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, \q o lugar onde {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} moras é tão querido para mim!

decisions.choice: a pilgrim's song
decisions.reason: The psalm is the song of someone who longs for the temple in Jerusalem (verses 3-5) and makes the journey there (verses 6-8), like Psalms 42-43, also of the sons of Korah.

decisions.choice: beloved: dearly loved
decisions.reason: The word (yadid) means beloved, as Benjamin is "the beloved of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 33:12). The temple is loved because God lives there.

decisions.choice: your dwellings: God's dwelling place
decisions.reason: The plural (mishkenot) is often used for a single dwelling, as in 43:3 and 46:5.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: The title (YHWH tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: to me
decisions.reason: Readable names who loves the place, the psalmist, as verse 3 does.

decisions.choice: "SEIGNEUR des armées" at every level, for Psalms 84-104
decisions.reason: The English says "of hosts" at Literal and "of Armies" at Balanced and Readable. French "armées" covers both the heavenly hosts and armies, and is the word a French reader knows in this title, so one form serves every level.

decisions.choice: "BWANA wa majeshi" at every level, for "LORD of hosts" (L) and "LORD of Armies" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Majeshi" means both the armies of a people and the hosts of heaven, so one Swahili word covers what the English says two ways at its levels. Swahili marks God's pronouns mostly inside the verb, so a deity_pronoun span stands only on free pronouns and possessives such as "yako".

decisions.choice: SEÑOR de los ejércitos (L); SEÑOR de los Ejércitos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The title YHWH tseba'ot names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven and of his people. Spanish "ejércitos" carries both the older English "hosts" and "Armies". Balanced and Readable write it with a capital, as a title, as the English does with "Armies". The same form is used in the psalms that follow.

decisions.choice: tú
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks to God with "tú", the ordinary second person of prayer in Spanish, close and direct as the Hebrew is. The pronoun takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Vạn Quân" and "Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân" at every level, as James 5:4
decisions.reason: The title names the LORD as the commander of armies. Literal says it word for word; Balanced and Readable use "Vạn Quân" (of ten thousand armies), the short form Vietnamese Bible readers know, as the English says "of Armies". It is used so through this block of psalms.

decisions.choice: The psalm speaks to God in 합쇼체 (here the polite exclamation "-ㄴ지요"), addresses him by the title "주님" and by name as "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여"; there are no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 7a) and the published Psalm 139: Korean speaks to a superior by title, not by a pronoun, and respect is carried by 주님, 께서 and -시-, so there is nothing for the English capitalisation setting to change. Where the psalmist speaks about God (verses 6-8, 12) the plain written style with the honorific is used. The singer is "저/제" when speaking to God. This holds for Psalms 84-104.

decisions.choice: "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}" (L, B); "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}" (R)
decisions.reason: The title means the LORD who commands the armies of heaven (the English decision). "만군" is the established Korean word for these hosts, used in the Korean James 5:4; Readable says what it means. The particle stands outside the divine_name span, which holds for the whole block.

decisions.choice: Quão amadas (L); Quão amáveis (B); as tuas moradas
decisions.reason: Literal says "amadas", the sense of yadid, "beloved" (m2); Balanced "amáveis", worthy of love, the word by which Portuguese readers know the opening of this psalm. "Moradas" keeps the Hebrew plural for God's one dwelling (m3) without the technical "tabernáculo", which the Old Testament terms keep for the tent of Exodus.

source.text: נִכְסְפָ֬ה וְגַם־כָּלְתָ֨ה׀נַפְשִׁי֮ לְחַצְר֪וֹת יְה֫וָ֥ה לִבִּ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֑י יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ אֶ֣ל אֵֽל־חָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My soul has longed and also fainted for [the] courts of YHWH; my heart and my flesh shout for joy to [the] living God.

en.L: My soul has longed and even fainted for the courts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q my heart and my flesh \q shout for joy to the living God.
en.B: My whole being longs, even aches, for the courts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q heart and body, \q I shout with joy to the living God.
en.R: I want so much to be in the courtyards of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house that I feel weak. \q With all my heart and body I sing for joy to the God who lives.

fr.L: Mon âme a langui et même défailli pour les parvis {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; \q mon cœur et ma chair \q crient de joie vers le Dieu vivant.
fr.B: Tout mon être soupire, il se meurt d’envie des parvis {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; \q de cœur et de corps, \q je crie de joie vers le Dieu vivant.
fr.R: J’ai tellement envie d’être dans les cours de la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} que je m’en sens faible. \q De tout mon cœur et de tout mon corps, je chante de joie pour le Dieu qui est vivant.

sw.L: Nafsi yangu imetamani, hata imezimia, kwa nyua za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q moyo wangu na mwili wangu \q vinapiga kelele za furaha kwa Mungu aliye hai.
sw.B: Mimi mzima ninatamani, hata kuzimia, nyua za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q kwa moyo na mwili \q ninapiga kelele za furaha kwa Mungu aliye hai.
sw.R: Ninatamani sana kuwa katika viwanja vya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, hata ninaishiwa nguvu. \q Kwa moyo wangu wote na mwili wangu ninamwimbia kwa furaha Mungu aliye hai.

es.L: Ha anhelado y aun desfallecido mi alma por los atrios {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; \q mi corazón y mi carne \q gritan de júbilo al Dios vivo.
es.B: Todo mi ser anhela, y hasta se consume, por los atrios {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; \q con el corazón y con el cuerpo \q grito de alegría al Dios vivo.
es.R: Deseo tanto estar en los patios de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que me siento débil. \q Con todo mi corazón y mi cuerpo canto de alegría al Dios que vive.

vi.L: Linh hồn tôi đã mong mỏi, và còn mòn mỏi, vì các sân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q lòng tôi và xác thịt tôi \q reo hò vui mừng với Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống.
vi.B: Cả con người tôi khao khát, thậm chí héo hon, mong đến các sân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q cả lòng và thân xác, \q tôi reo mừng với Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống.
vi.R: Tôi ao ước được ở trong sân nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến nỗi thấy mình kiệt sức. \q Với cả tấm lòng và thân thể, tôi hát vui mừng cho Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng đang sống.

ko.L: 내 영혼이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 뜰을 사모하다가 지치기까지 하였으니, \q 내 마음과 내 육체가 \q 살아 계신 하나님께 기뻐 외칩니다.
ko.B: 내 온 존재가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 뜰을 그리워하다 못해 애가 탑니다. \q 몸과 마음을 다하여 \q 살아 계신 하나님께 기뻐 외칩니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집 뜰에 너무나 가고 싶어서 힘이 빠질 지경입니다. \q 온 마음과 온몸으로 살아 계신 하나님께 기쁘게 노래합니다.

pt.L: A minha alma anseia e até desfalece pelos átrios {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; \q o meu coração e a minha carne \q gritam de alegria ao Deus vivo.
pt.B: Todo o meu ser anseia, chega a desfalecer, pelos átrios {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; \q de coração e corpo, \q grito de alegria ao Deus vivo.
pt.R: Quero tanto estar nos pátios da casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} que chego a me sentir fraco. \q Com todo o meu coração e todo o meu corpo, canto de alegria ao Deus que vive.

decisions.choice: my soul: my whole self
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the living self, with its desires (42:2-3).

decisions.choice: the courts: the temple courtyards
decisions.reason: Worshipers gathered in the open courtyards around the temple building; only priests went inside (65:5; 100:4).

decisions.choice: shout for joy to: cry out to
alternatives: cry out for the living God
decisions.reason: The verb (ranan) is usually a ringing shout of joy. With "to" it may also mean a loud cry of longing for God, as in 42:3.

decisions.choice: the living God
decisions.reason: God is alive and acts, unlike idols (42:3; Joshua 3:10).

decisions.choice: my whole being (B); I (R)
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Balanced and Readable render nefesh as the self.

decisions.choice: "mon âme" at Literal for nefesh; "tout mon être" (Balanced) and "je" (Readable)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: "âme" at Literal keeps the Hebrew word, while Balanced and Readable say the whole person, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nafsi yangu" (my soul) at Literal; "mimi mzima" (all of me) at Balanced and plain "I" at Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew nefesh is the whole living self. Literal keeps the word "nafsi"; Balanced and Readable say the person, as the English does. "Roho" would suggest the spirit as distinct from the body, which the verse goes on to join together.

decisions.choice: mi alma (L); todo mi ser (B); yo (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew nefesh is the living self with its desires. Literal keeps "alma"; Balanced says "todo mi ser" and Readable simply "I", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "linh hồn tôi" (L); "cả con người tôi" (B); "tôi" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (nefesh) is the whole living self (see the meaning decision). Literal keeps the familiar word; Balanced and Readable say the self, as the English does. The block follows this wherever the word means the person.

decisions.choice: "내 영혼" (L), "내 온 존재" (B), the plain subject (R) for nefesh; the singer says "내" here, between lines addressed to God
decisions.reason: "영혼" is the term note's word at Literal; Balanced and Readable say the whole self, as the English does (meaning decision m1). The verse speaks about the LORD in the third person, so the singer's "내" belongs to the plain voice; Korean poetry allows the first-person 나 in a line not spoken to God.

source.text: גַּם־צִפּ֨וֹר׀מָ֪צְאָה בַ֡יִת וּדְר֤וֹר׀קֵ֥ן לָהּ֮ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֪תָה אֶפְרֹ֫חֶ֥יהָ אֶֽת־מִ֭זְבְּחוֹתֶיךָ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מַ֝לְכִּ֗י וֵאלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Even [the] bird has found a house, and [the] swallow a nest for herself, where she has put her young: your altars, YHWH of hosts, my King and my God.

en.L: Even the bird has found a house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she has put her young: \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q my King and my God.
en.B: The sparrow, too, has found itself a home, and the swallow has a nest where it keeps its young, \q beside {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q my King and my God.
en.R: Even little birds have found homes there. \q They make nests for their babies near {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q my King and my God.

fr.L: Même l’oiseau a trouvé une maison, et l’hirondelle un nid pour elle, où elle a mis ses petits : \q {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q mon Roi et mon Dieu.
fr.B: Le moineau lui aussi s’est trouvé un logis, et l’hirondelle un nid où elle garde ses petits, \q près de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q mon Roi et mon Dieu.
fr.R: Même les petits oiseaux y ont trouvé une maison. \q Ils font leur nid pour leurs petits près de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} autels, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q mon Roi et mon Dieu.

sw.L: Hata ndege amepata nyumba, na mbayuwayu kiota chake, alipoweka makinda yake: \q madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q Mfalme wangu na Mungu wangu.
sw.B: Shomoro naye amejipatia makao, na mbayuwayu ana kiota anapowatunza makinda yake, \q karibu na madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q Mfalme wangu na Mungu wangu.
sw.R: Hata ndege wadogo wamepata makao huko. \q Wanajenga viota kwa ajili ya makinda yao karibu na madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q Mfalme wangu na Mungu wangu.

es.L: Aun el pájaro ha hallado casa, y la golondrina nido para sí, donde ha puesto sus crías: \q {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, \q Rey mío y Dios mío.
es.B: También el gorrión se ha hallado un hogar, y la golondrina tiene un nido donde guarda a sus polluelos, \q junto a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q mi Rey y mi Dios.
es.R: Hasta los pajaritos han encontrado allí un hogar. \q Hacen nidos para sus crías cerca de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} altares, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q mi Rey y mi Dios.

vi.L: Ngay cả con chim cũng đã tìm được một cái nhà, và chim én [tìm được] một cái tổ cho mình, nơi nó đặt con nhỏ của nó: \q [là] các bàn thờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q Vua của tôi và Đức Chúa Trời của tôi.
vi.B: Chim sẻ cũng đã tìm được chỗ ở, và chim én có tổ để nuôi con nhỏ, \q bên cạnh các bàn thờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q là Vua tôi và Đức Chúa Trời tôi.
vi.R: Ngay cả những con chim nhỏ cũng tìm được chỗ ở tại đó. \q Chúng làm tổ cho chim con gần các bàn thờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q là Vua tôi và Đức Chúa Trời tôi.

ko.L: 새도 집을 찾았고, 제비도 제 새끼를 둘 보금자리를 얻었습니다. \q 그곳은 주님의 제단들, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, \q 나의 왕, 나의 하나님이시여.
ko.B: 참새도 제 집을 찾았고, 제비도 새끼 칠 둥지를 얻었습니다. \q 주님의 제단 곁에서입니다, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, \q 저의 왕, 저의 하나님이시여.
ko.R: 작은 새들도 거기에 집을 마련했습니다. \q 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 새들이 주님의 제단 가까이에 새끼들을 위한 둥지를 틉니다. \q 주님은 저의 왕, 저의 하나님이십니다.

pt.L: Até o pássaro encontrou uma casa, e a andorinha um ninho para si, onde pôs os seus filhotes: \q os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} altares, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, \q meu Rei e meu Deus.
pt.B: Também o pardal encontrou um lar, e a andorinha tem um ninho onde guarda os seus filhotes, \q junto aos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} altares, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, \q meu Rei e meu Deus.
pt.R: Até os passarinhos encontraram casa ali. \q Eles fazem ninhos para os seus filhotes perto dos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} altares, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, \q meu Rei e meu Deus.

decisions.choice: the bird ... the swallow
decisions.reason: The first word (tsippor) is any small bird, often the sparrow; the second (deror) is probably the swallow (Proverbs 26:2).

decisions.choice: your altars: near the altars
decisions.reason: The birds nest near the altars, in the temple courts. The words may also be the psalmist's cry: the birds have their homes, and I long for your altars.

decisions.choice: your altars: the two altars of the temple
decisions.reason: The temple had an altar for burnt offerings in the courtyard and an altar for incense inside.

decisions.choice: my King: God as king
decisions.reason: As in 5:3, God is the psalmist's king.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: The title (YHWH tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.

source.text: אַ֭שְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י בֵיתֶ֑ךָ ע֝֗וֹד יְֽהַלְל֥וּךָ סֶּֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [are those who] dwell [in] your house; still they praise you. Selah.

en.L: How blessed [are those who] dwell [in] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house; \q they still praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Selah
en.B: How blessed are the ones who live in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house; \q they never stop praising {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Selah
en.R: Life is truly good for those who live in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house. \q They praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all the time. Selah

fr.L: Heureux ceux qui habitent {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison ; \q encore ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} louent. Sélah
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui habitent dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison ; \q ils ne cessent de {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} louer. Sélah
fr.R: Ceux qui vivent dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison sont vraiment heureux. \q Ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} louent tout le temps. Sélah

sw.L: Heri [wale] wakaao [katika] nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}; \q bado wanakusifu. Sela
sw.B: Heri wale wanaoishi katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}; \q hawaachi kukusifu. Sela
sw.R: Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa wale wanaoishi katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. \q Wanakusifu wakati wote. Sela

es.L: Dichosos [los que] habitan [en] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} casa; \q aún {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} alaban. Selah
es.B: ¡Qué dichosos son los que viven en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} casa! \q Nunca dejan de alabarte. Selah
es.R: Qué buena es la vida de los que viven en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} casa. \q Te alaban todo el tiempo. Selah

vi.L: Phước thay [những người] ở [trong] nhà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q họ vẫn ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la
vi.B: Phước hạnh thay những người được sống trong nhà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q họ không ngừng ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la
vi.R: Thật hạnh phúc cho những người sống trong nhà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Họ luôn luôn ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la

ko.L: 주님의 집에 사는 사람들은 얼마나 복된지요. \q 그들은 여전히 주님을 찬양합니다. 셀라
ko.B: 주님의 집에 사는 사람들은 얼마나 복됩니까! \q 그들은 쉬지 않고 주님을 찬양합니다. 셀라
ko.R: 주님의 집에서 사는 사람들은 참으로 행복합니다. \q 그들은 언제나 주님을 찬양합니다. 셀라

pt.L: Bem-aventurados os que habitam [na] {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} casa; \q eles ainda {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} louvam. Selá
pt.B: Como são felizes os que moram na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} casa; \q eles nunca param de {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} louvar. Selá
pt.R: Felizes de verdade são os que moram na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} casa. \q Eles {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} louvam o tempo todo. Selá

decisions.choice: those who dwell in your house: the temple servants
alternatives: all who worship at the temple
decisions.reason: Those who live in God's house are probably the priests and Levites who serve there day by day, or anyone who stays near God in worship (23:6; 27:4).

decisions.choice: how blessed: truly happy
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, the word ('ashre) describes a life that is truly good.

decisions.choice: still: continually
decisions.reason: The word ('od) means "yet" or "still": their praise goes on.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: "Sélah", kept at the end of the verse at every level
decisions.reason: The word's meaning is no longer known (meaning decision); it is probably a musical direction. French keeps it in its usual French spelling, as the English keeps "Selah".

decisions.choice: "Heureux" for ʾashrey at Literal and Balanced; "vraiment heureux" at Readable
decisions.reason: The word says how well off a person is, not that God pronounces a blessing, as in Proverbs. "Heureux" is the plain French.

decisions.choice: "Heri" (L, B) for how blessed; "Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa" (life is truly good for) at Readable
decisions.reason: "Heri" is the Swahili word that pronounces someone truly happy; it is not "barikiwa", which would say God has blessed them. Readable spells it out, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Sela" kept at the end of the verse at every level
decisions.reason: Selah is a Hebrew word whose meaning is no longer known, probably a musical direction. Swahili keeps it in its Swahili spelling, as the English keeps it, rather than guess at a translation.

decisions.choice: dichosos (L, B); Qué buena es la vida de (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew ashre ("how blessed") describes a life that goes well with God. Literal and Balanced say "dichosos", the everyday Spanish word; Readable says that their life is good, as the English Readable says "Life is truly good for".

decisions.choice: Selah
decisions.reason: Selah is a Hebrew word whose meaning is no longer known; it is probably a direction for the music or the singers. Spanish keeps it as it is, at the end of the verse, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Phước thay" (L), "Phước hạnh thay" (B), "Thật hạnh phúc cho" (R), as Psalm 1:1
decisions.reason: The cry is about a life that goes well (see the meaning decision). "Phước thay" keeps the short exclamation; Readable uses the everyday "hạnh phúc" (happy, well off), as the English Readable says "Life is truly good".

decisions.choice: "Sê-la" kept at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: No one now knows what Selah means; it is probably a direction for the music (see the meaning decision). Vietnamese keeps the word, in the form Bible readers know, wherever the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: "셀라", kept at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: Selah is a word whose meaning is no longer known, probably a musical direction (meaning decision m4). Korean keeps it as a name, as the English keeps "Selah", in the form Korean readers know. This holds wherever it appears in Psalms 84-104.

decisions.choice: "참으로 행복합니다" for ashrei at Readable; "복되다" at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Readable says what the blessing means in plain words, as the English Readable "life is truly good" does (meaning decision m2), and as the published Psalm 1:1 Readable does.

source.text: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם עֽוֹז־ל֥וֹ בָ֑ךְ מְ֝סִלּ֗וֹת בִּלְבָבָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [is the] person [whose] strength [is] in you, highways in their heart.

en.L: How blessed [is the] {{gender:person|man}} whose strength [is] in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q [with] highways in their heart.
en.B: How blessed are people who find their strength in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} \q and fix their hearts on the pilgrim highways.
en.R: Life is truly good for people who get their strength from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q They love to travel on the roads to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house.

fr.L: {{gender:Heureuse la personne|Heureux l’homme}} dont la force [est] en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \q [avec] des routes dans son cœur.
fr.B: Heureux ceux qui trouvent leur force en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} \q et qui ont à cœur les routes du pèlerinage.
fr.R: Ceux qui reçoivent leur force de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} sont vraiment heureux. \q Ils aiment prendre les routes qui mènent à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison.

sw.L: Heri mtu ambaye nguvu yake [iko] {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}; \q [wenye] njia kuu mioyoni mwao.
sw.B: Heri watu wanaopata nguvu zao {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} \q na mioyo yao imeelekea njia kuu za kuhiji.
sw.R: Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa watu wanaopata nguvu kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. \q Wanapenda kusafiri katika njia ziendazo nyumbani {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}.

es.L: ¡{{gender:Dichosa la persona|Dichoso el hombre}} cuya fuerza [está] en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q [con] calzadas en su corazón!
es.B: ¡Qué dichosos son los que hallan su fuerza en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} \q y tienen el corazón puesto en los caminos de peregrinación!
es.R: Qué buena es la vida de los que reciben de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} su fuerza. \q Les encanta viajar por los caminos que llevan a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} casa.

vi.L: Phước thay người có sức mạnh ở trong {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q [có] những đại lộ trong lòng mình.
vi.B: Phước hạnh thay những người tìm được sức mạnh nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} \q và để lòng hướng về những con đường hành hương.
vi.R: Thật hạnh phúc cho những người nhận sức mạnh từ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Họ thích đi trên những con đường dẫn đến nhà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 주님 안에 힘이 있는 사람은 얼마나 복된지요, \q 그 마음에 큰길들이 [있는 사람은].
ko.B: 주님에게서 힘을 얻고 \q 순례의 길을 마음에 품은 사람들은 얼마나 복됩니까!
ko.R: 주님에게서 힘을 얻는 사람들은 참으로 행복합니다. \q 그들은 주님의 집으로 가는 길을 걷기를 좋아합니다.

pt.L: Bem-aventurado [é] {{gender:o ser humano|o homem}} cuja força [está] em {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q [com] estradas no seu coração.
pt.B: Como são felizes os que encontram a sua força em {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} \q e têm o coração posto nas estradas dos peregrinos.
pt.R: Felizes de verdade são as pessoas que recebem força de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. \q Elas adoram viajar pelos caminhos que levam à {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} casa.

decisions.choice: highways: the roads of pilgrimage
decisions.reason: The word (mesillot) is a built-up road. Here it is most likely the roads pilgrims took up to Jerusalem for the feasts: their hearts are set on the journey.

decisions.choice: a person ... their heart
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with one person ("to him") and goes on with "their heart": anyone, and all, who make the journey.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for the generic person, as the Hebrew itself does in the second half of the verse.

decisions.choice: they love to travel on the roads to your house
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

decisions.choice: the gender setting on the noun: "Heureuse la personne" by default, "Heureux l'homme" as the alternative
alternatives: a span on the pronoun, as the English "their"
decisions.reason: French puts the setting on the noun only; the possessive "son" is the same for both. The adjective agrees with the noun, so it goes inside the span: "Heureuse la personne" or "Heureux l'homme".

decisions.choice: "njia kuu za kuhiji" (the highways of pilgrimage) at Balanced
decisions.reason: The highways in the heart are the roads to the temple; "kuhiji" (to go on pilgrimage) says so in a word Swahili readers know, as the English "pilgrim highways" does.

decisions.choice: "người" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "người" already means anyone, man or woman, so Vietnamese has no second form for the English gender setting to switch to, as in Psalm 1:1.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "man" as an alternative to "person". Korean "사람" is the ordinary word for anyone, man or woman, so Korean has no second wording to offer (style guide section 7). This holds for the gender spans of the English through Psalms 84-104.

source.text: עֹבְרֵ֤י׀בְּעֵ֣מֶק הַ֭בָּכָא מַעְיָ֣ן יְשִׁית֑וּהוּ גַּם־בְּ֝רָכ֗וֹת יַעְטֶ֥ה מוֹרֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Passing through [the] valley of the Baca, a spring they make it; also blessings [the] early rain covers.

en.L: Passing through the valley of Baca, they make it a spring; \q the early rain also covers [it with] blessings.
en.B: When they travel through the Baca Valley, they make it a land of springs; \q the early rain wraps it in blessings.
en.R: On the road they pass through the Valley of Baca, and they turn it into a place where springs flow. \q The first rains cover it with blessings.

fr.L: Passant par la vallée de Baca, ils en font une source ; \q la pluie d’automne aussi [la] couvre de bénédictions.
fr.B: Quand ils traversent la vallée de Baca, ils en font un pays de sources ; \q la première pluie l’enveloppe de bénédictions.
fr.R: En chemin, ils passent par la vallée de Baca, et ils en font un lieu où coulent des sources. \q Les premières pluies la couvrent de bénédictions.

sw.L: Wakipita katika bonde la Baka, hulifanya kuwa chemchemi; \q mvua ya kwanza nayo hulifunika [kwa] baraka.
sw.B: Wanapopita katika Bonde la Baka, wanalifanya nchi ya chemchemi; \q mvua ya kwanza inalivika baraka.
sw.R: Njiani wanapita katika Bonde la Baka, nalo linageuka mahali penye chemchemi za maji. \q Mvua za kwanza zinalifunika kwa baraka.

es.L: Pasando por el valle de Baca, lo convierten en manantial; \q también la lluvia temprana [lo] cubre [de] bendiciones.
es.B: Cuando cruzan el valle de Baca, lo hacen tierra de manantiales; \q la lluvia temprana lo envuelve en bendiciones.
es.R: En el camino pasan por el valle de Baca, y lo convierten en un lugar donde brotan fuentes. \q Las primeras lluvias lo cubren de bendiciones.

vi.L: Khi đi qua thung lũng Ba-ca, họ làm cho nó thành một dòng suối; \q mưa đầu mùa cũng phủ [nó bằng] những phước lành.
vi.B: Khi đi ngang qua thung lũng Ba-ca, họ biến nơi ấy thành vùng đất có nhiều suối nước; \q mưa đầu mùa bao phủ nơi ấy bằng phước lành.
vi.R: Trên đường đi, họ băng qua thung lũng Ba-ca và biến nơi ấy thành chỗ có suối nước chảy. \q Những cơn mưa đầu mùa phủ đầy phước lành trên nơi ấy.

ko.L: 바카 골짜기를 지나가며 그들이 그곳을 샘으로 만들고, \q 이른 비도 [그곳을] 복으로 덮습니다.
ko.B: 그들이 바카 골짜기를 지날 때 그곳은 샘이 솟는 땅이 되고, \q 이른 비가 그곳을 복으로 감쌉니다.
ko.R: 그들은 가는 길에 바카 골짜기를 지나는데, 그곳을 샘물이 흐르는 곳으로 바꾸어 놓습니다. \q 첫 비가 내려 그곳을 복으로 덮습니다.

pt.L: Passando pelo vale de Baca, fazem dele uma fonte; \q também a chuva temporã [o] cobre de bênçãos.
pt.B: Quando atravessam o vale de Baca, fazem dele uma terra de fontes; \q a primeira chuva o envolve de bênçãos.
pt.R: No caminho, eles passam pelo vale de Baca e o transformam num lugar onde correm fontes. \q As primeiras chuvas cobrem o vale de bênçãos.

decisions.choice: Baca: a dry valley, or the valley of weeping
decisions.reason: Baca is not otherwise known as a place. The word names a kind of tree or shrub (2 Samuel 5) that grows in dry places, and it sounds like the word for weeping. Either way it is a hard stretch of the road, made a place of springs.

decisions.choice: blessings: the vowels as they stand
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew letters can be read "blessings" (berakhot) or "pools" (berekhot). The vowels of the Hebrew text give "blessings"; the rain covers the valley with good things.

decisions.choice: the early rain: the first autumn rain
decisions.reason: The first rains fell in October and November, after the dry summer, softening the ground for sowing (Deuteronomy 11:14).

decisions.choice: "바카" kept as a name
decisions.reason: The name may mean a dry valley or the valley of weeping (meaning decision m1); Korean keeps the name, as the English does, and does not choose between the senses.

source.text: יֵ֭לְכוּ מֵחַ֣יִל אֶל־חָ֑יִל יֵרָאֶ֖ה אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים בְּצִיּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: They go from strength to strength; he appears before God in Zion.

en.L: They go from strength to strength; \q [each one] appears before God in Zion.
en.B: They walk on from strength to strength, \q till every one of them comes before God in Zion.
en.R: They get stronger and stronger as they go, \q until they all stand before God in Zion.

fr.L: Ils vont de force en force ; \q [chacun] paraît devant Dieu en Sion.
fr.B: Ils avancent de force en force, \q jusqu’à ce que chacun d’eux se présente devant Dieu en Sion.
fr.R: Plus ils marchent, plus ils deviennent forts, \q jusqu’à ce qu’ils soient tous devant Dieu, à Sion.

sw.L: Wanakwenda kutoka nguvu hadi nguvu; \q [kila mmoja] anatokea mbele za Mungu katika Sayuni.
sw.B: Wanaendelea kutoka nguvu hadi nguvu, \q mpaka kila mmoja wao afike mbele za Mungu katika Sayuni.
sw.R: Wanazidi kupata nguvu kadiri wanavyosafiri, \q mpaka wote wasimame mbele za Mungu katika Sayuni.

es.L: Van de fuerza en fuerza; \q [cada uno] se presenta ante Dios en Sion.
es.B: Caminan de fuerza en fuerza, \q hasta que cada uno de ellos llega ante Dios en Sion.
es.R: Se hacen más y más fuertes mientras avanzan, \q hasta que todos están delante de Dios en Sion.

vi.L: Họ đi từ sức mạnh đến sức mạnh; \q [mỗi người] ra mắt Đức Chúa Trời tại Si-ôn.
vi.B: Họ cứ đi, sức mạnh càng thêm sức mạnh, \q cho đến khi mỗi người đến trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời tại Si-ôn.
vi.R: Họ càng đi càng mạnh mẽ hơn, \q cho đến khi tất cả đứng trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời tại Si-ôn.

ko.L: 그들은 힘에서 힘으로 나아가, \q [각 사람이] 시온에서 하나님 앞에 나타납니다.
ko.B: 그들은 갈수록 힘을 얻어 걸어가서, \q 마침내 모두가 시온에서 하나님 앞에 섭니다.
ko.R: 그들은 갈수록 더 힘이 납니다. \q 그리고 마침내 모두 시온에서 하나님 앞에 섭니다.

pt.L: Vão de força em força; \q [cada um] se apresenta diante de Deus em Sião.
pt.B: Seguem caminhando de força em força, \q até que cada um deles se apresente diante de Deus em Sião.
pt.R: Ficam cada vez mais fortes enquanto caminham, \q até que todos estão diante de Deus em Sião.

decisions.choice: from strength to strength: growing stronger
decisions.reason: Instead of tiring on the road, the pilgrims gain strength as they near Zion (Isaiah 40:31).

decisions.choice: appears before God: comes to the festival
decisions.reason: Every Israelite man was to appear before the LORD three times a year at the feasts (Exodus 23:17; Deuteronomy 16:16).

decisions.choice: before God: the Hebrew text
alternatives: the God of gods will be seen in Zion (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation read the same letters as "the God of gods will be seen in Zion". The Hebrew text as it stands says the pilgrim appears before God.

decisions.choice: every one of them (B); they all (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is singular: each one of the pilgrims.

source.text: יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְ֭בָאוֹת שִׁמְעָ֣ה תְפִלָּתִ֑י הַאֲזִ֨ינָה אֱלֹהֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH God hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, God of Jacob! Selah.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts, hear my prayer; \q give ear, God of Jacob! Selah
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, hear my prayer; \q turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to me, God of Jacob! Selah
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, listen as I pray. \q Hear me, God of Jacob's people! Selah

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu des armées, écoute ma prière ; \q prête l’oreille, Dieu de Jacob ! Sélah
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu des armées, écoute ma prière ; \q tends l’oreille vers moi, Dieu de Jacob ! Sélah
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu des armées, écoute-moi quand je prie. \q Entends-moi, Dieu du peuple de Jacob ! Sélah

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, sikia maombi yangu; \q tega sikio, Ee Mungu wa Yakobo! Sela
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, sikia maombi yangu; \q nitegee sikio {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, Ee Mungu wa Yakobo! Sela
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, unisikilize ninapoomba. \q Unisikie, Ee Mungu wa watu wa Yakobo! Sela

es.L: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos, escucha mi oración; \q presta oído, Dios de Jacob. Selah
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos, escucha mi oración; \q inclina {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} oído hacia mí, Dios de Jacob. Selah
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos, escucha cuando oro. \q Óyeme, Dios del pueblo de Jacob. Selah

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, xin nghe lời cầu nguyện của tôi; \q xin lắng tai, lạy Đức Chúa Trời của Gia-cốp! Sê-la
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, xin nghe lời tôi cầu nguyện; \q lạy Đức Chúa Trời của Gia-cốp, xin nghiêng tai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe tôi! Sê-la
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, xin lắng nghe khi tôi cầu nguyện. \q Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của dân Gia-cốp, xin nghe tôi! Sê-la

ko.L: 만군의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제 기도를 들어 주십시오. \q 야곱의 하나님이시여, 귀를 기울여 주십시오! 셀라
ko.B: 만군의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제 기도를 들어 주십시오. \q 야곱의 하나님이시여, 제게 귀를 기울여 주십시오! 셀라
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 기도하오니 들어 주십시오. \q 야곱 자손의 하나님이시여, 제 말을 들어 주십시오! 셀라

pt.L: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} Deus dos Exércitos, ouve a minha oração; \q presta ouvidos, Deus de Jacó! Selá
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus dos Exércitos, ouve a minha oração; \q inclina para mim o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ouvido, Deus de Jacó! Selá
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus dos Exércitos, escuta enquanto eu oro. \q Ouve-me, Deus do povo de Jacó! Selá

decisions.choice: LORD God of hosts
decisions.reason: The same chain of names as in 80:5.

decisions.choice: LORD God of Armies
decisions.reason: As with "the LORD of hosts", the title names God as commander of the armies of heaven and of his people. Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies".

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: "xin" before each request to God, unbracketed at Literal
decisions.reason: A bare command to God is rude in Vietnamese; "xin" is the word of request that the grammar of prayer requires, like "Lạy" in the address, so Literal does not bracket it.

source.text: מָ֭גִנֵּנוּ רְאֵ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְ֝הַבֵּ֗ט פְּנֵ֣י מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Our shield see, God, and look at [the] face of your anointed.

en.L: Our shield, see, God, \q and look at the face of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed.
en.B: God, see our shield; \q look with care on the face of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed one.
en.R: God, look at the king who protects us like a shield. \q Be kind to the king {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen.

fr.L: Notre bouclier, vois, ô Dieu, \q et regarde la face de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} oint.
fr.B: Ô Dieu, vois notre bouclier ; \q regarde avec bonté le visage de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} oint.
fr.R: Ô Dieu, regarde le roi qui nous protège comme un bouclier. \q Sois bon pour le roi que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as choisi.

sw.L: Ngao yetu, tazama, Ee Mungu, \q na uutazame uso wa mpakwa mafuta {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Ee Mungu, uitazame ngao yetu; \q uutazame kwa makini uso wa mpakwa mafuta {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.R: Ee Mungu, mtazame mfalme anayetulinda kama ngao. \q Mwonyeshe wema mfalme uliyemchagua.

es.L: Escudo nuestro, mira, oh Dios, \q y contempla el rostro de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ungido.
es.B: Oh Dios, mira a nuestro escudo; \q contempla con bondad el rostro de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ungido.
es.R: Dios, mira al rey que nos protege como un escudo. \q Sé bondadoso con el rey que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has escogido.

vi.L: Cái khiên của chúng tôi, xin hãy xem, lạy Đức Chúa Trời, \q và xin nhìn mặt của người được xức dầu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, xin đoái xem cái khiên của chúng tôi; \q xin ân cần nhìn đến mặt người được xức dầu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, xin đoái xem vị vua đang bảo vệ chúng tôi như cái khiên. \q Xin tỏ lòng tốt với vị vua mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn.

ko.L: 저희의 방패를 보십시오, 하나님, \q 주님의 기름 부음 받은 이의 얼굴을 살펴 주십시오.
ko.B: 하나님, 저희의 방패를 보아 주십시오. \q 주님께서 기름 부으신 이의 얼굴을 돌보아 주십시오.
ko.R: 하나님, 방패처럼 저희를 지켜 주는 왕을 보아 주십시오. \q 주님께서 세우신 왕에게 은혜를 베풀어 주십시오.

pt.L: O nosso escudo, vê, Deus, \q e olha para o rosto do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ungido.
pt.B: Deus, vê o nosso escudo; \q olha com bondade para o rosto do {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ungido.
pt.R: Deus, olha para o rei que nos protege como um escudo. \q Sê bondoso com o rei que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} escolheste.

decisions.choice: our shield: the king
alternatives: God, our shield, look (on your anointed)
decisions.reason: "Our shield" is most likely the king, named again in the second half as God's anointed (47:10; 89:19). It can also be read as a title for God: "see, God our shield".

decisions.choice: your anointed: the king
decisions.reason: The anointed one (mashiach) is the king of Israel, anointed with oil when he took the throne (2:2; 18:51). The pilgrims pray for him.

decisions.choice: look at the face: look with favor
decisions.reason: To look at someone's face is to give him a favorable hearing.

decisions.choice: the king who protects us like a shield; the king you have chosen
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "mpakwa mafuta wako" (your anointed one) at Literal and Balanced; "mfalme uliyemchagua" (the king you chose) at Readable
decisions.reason: Here the anointed is the king of Israel, so the plain description "mpakwa mafuta" fits better than "masihi", which most Swahili readers hear as the title of Jesus. Readable says who is meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: el ungido
decisions.reason: The Hebrew mashiach here is the king of Israel, anointed with oil. Spanish says "ungido", the plain word for one anointed, so that the reader does not take it as a later title; Readable says "el rey", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "기름 부음 받은 이" (L), "주님께서 기름 부으신 이" (B); "주님께서 세우신 왕" (R)
decisions.reason: The anointed is the king (meaning decision m2); the term note's "기름 부음 받은 이" keeps the Hebrew picture at Literal and Balanced, and Readable names the king, as the English Readable does.

source.text: כִּ֤י טֽוֹב־י֥וֹם בַּחֲצֵרֶ֗יךָ מֵ֫אָ֥לֶף בָּחַ֗רְתִּי הִ֭סְתּוֹפֵף בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהַ֑י מִ֝דּ֗וּר בְּאָהֳלֵי־רֶֽשַׁע׃

records.literal_gloss: For better [is] a day in your courts than a thousand; I have chosen standing at the threshold in [the] house of my God than dwelling in [the] tents of wickedness.

en.L: For better [is] a day in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courts than a thousand; \q I have chosen to stand at the threshold in the house of my God \q rather than to dwell in [the] tents of wickedness.
en.B: Truly, one day spent in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courts is worth more than a thousand anywhere else; \q I would choose to stand at the threshold of my God's house \q over living in the tents of wicked people.
en.R: Spending one day in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courtyards is better than spending a thousand days somewhere else. \q I would rather stand at the door of my God's house \q than live in the homes of evil people.

fr.L: Car mieux [vaut] un jour dans {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} parvis que mille ; \q j’ai choisi de me tenir sur le seuil dans la maison de mon Dieu \q plutôt que d’habiter dans [les] tentes de la méchanceté.
fr.B: Oui, un seul jour passé dans {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} parvis vaut mieux que mille ailleurs ; \q je préfère me tenir sur le seuil de la maison de mon Dieu \q plutôt que de vivre sous les tentes des méchants.
fr.R: Passer un jour dans les cours de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison vaut mieux que passer mille jours ailleurs. \q J’aime mieux me tenir à la porte de la maison de mon Dieu \q que vivre chez des gens mauvais.

sw.L: Kwa maana siku moja katika nyua {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} [ni] bora kuliko elfu; \q nimechagua kusimama kizingitini katika nyumba ya Mungu wangu \q kuliko kukaa katika hema za uovu.
sw.B: Kweli, siku moja katika nyua {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} ni bora kuliko siku elfu mahali pengine; \q ningechagua kusimama kizingitini mwa nyumba ya Mungu wangu \q kuliko kuishi katika hema za waovu.
sw.R: Kukaa siku moja katika viwanja {{deity_pronoun:vyako|Vyako}} ni bora kuliko kukaa siku elfu mahali pengine. \q Ningependa zaidi kusimama mlangoni mwa nyumba ya Mungu wangu \q kuliko kuishi katika nyumba za watu waovu.

es.L: Porque mejor [es] un día en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} atrios que mil; \q he escogido estar en el umbral en la casa de mi Dios \q antes que habitar en [las] tiendas de maldad.
es.B: De verdad, un día en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} atrios vale más que mil en cualquier otro lugar; \q prefiero estar en el umbral de la casa de mi Dios \q antes que vivir en las tiendas de los malvados.
es.R: Pasar un día en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} patios es mejor que pasar mil días en otra parte. \q Prefiero estar a la puerta de la casa de mi Dios \q que vivir en las casas de la gente mala.

vi.L: Vì một ngày trong các sân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tốt hơn cả nghìn [ngày]; \q tôi đã chọn đứng nơi ngưỡng cửa trong nhà Đức Chúa Trời của tôi \q hơn là ở trong [các] lều của sự gian ác.
vi.B: Thật vậy, một ngày ở trong các sân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quý hơn cả nghìn ngày ở nơi khác; \q tôi thà đứng nơi ngưỡng cửa nhà Đức Chúa Trời tôi \q còn hơn sống trong lều trại của kẻ ác.
vi.R: Được ở một ngày trong sân nhà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn tốt hơn ở một nghìn ngày nơi khác. \q Tôi thà đứng ở cửa nhà Đức Chúa Trời tôi \q còn hơn sống trong nhà của những kẻ gian ác.

ko.L: 참으로 주님의 뜰에서의 하루가 천 [날]보다 낫습니다. \q 제 하나님의 집 문지방에 서 있기를 택하겠습니다, \q 악의 장막들에 사는 것보다.
ko.B: 참으로 주님의 뜰에서 보내는 하루가 다른 곳에서 보내는 천 날보다 낫습니다. \q 악한 사람들의 장막에서 사는 것보다 \q 차라리 제 하나님의 집 문간에 서 있기를 택하겠습니다.
ko.R: 주님의 집 뜰에서 하루를 보내는 것이 다른 곳에서 천 날을 보내는 것보다 낫습니다. \q 악한 사람들의 집에서 사는 것보다 \q 차라리 제 하나님의 집 문 앞에 서 있겠습니다.

pt.L: Pois melhor [é] um dia nos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} átrios do que mil; \q escolhi ficar à porta na casa do meu Deus \q a habitar nas tendas da impiedade.
pt.B: Na verdade, um dia passado nos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} átrios vale mais que mil em qualquer outro lugar; \q eu preferiria ficar à porta da casa do meu Deus \q a morar nas tendas dos ímpios.
pt.R: Passar um dia nos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} pátios é melhor do que passar mil dias em outro lugar. \q Eu preferiria ficar na porta da casa do meu Deus \q a viver na casa de gente má.

decisions.choice: stand at the threshold: wait at the door
decisions.reason: The verb (histofef) is found only here and comes from the word for a threshold. It may mean to keep the door, as the sons of Korah did (1 Chronicles 9:19), or simply to stand at the entrance. Even the humblest place near God is better.

decisions.choice: than a thousand: a thousand days elsewhere
decisions.reason: "Days" is understood from the first half of the line.

decisions.choice: tents of wickedness: the homes of the wicked
decisions.reason: Tents stand for homes and households (83:7).

decisions.choice: anywhere else (B); somewhere else (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the thousand days are spent (m2).

decisions.choice: The comparison ("악한 사람들의 장막에서 사는 것보다") comes before the choice at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps the Hebrew order with the comparison after
alternatives: the Hebrew order at every level
decisions.reason: Korean puts the standard of comparison ("-보다") before what is preferred; Literal, as poetry allows, leaves it at the end so the lines follow the Hebrew's cola in order.

source.text: כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ׀וּמָגֵן֮ יְהוָ֪ה אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים חֵ֣ן וְ֭כָבוֹד יִתֵּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֥א יִמְנַע־ט֝֗וֹב לַֽהֹלְכִ֥ים בְּתָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For a sun and a shield [is] YHWH God; favor and honor gives YHWH; not he withholds good from [those who] walk in blamelessness.

en.L: For a sun and a shield [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God; \q favor and honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not withhold good from those who walk in blamelessness.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God is both sun and shield; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives favor and honor; \q from those who walk blamelessly {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps back nothing good.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God gives light like the sun and protects like a shield. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} shows kindness and gives honor. \q He does not hold back anything good from people who live without blame.

fr.L: Car un soleil et un bouclier, [c’est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu ; \q la faveur et la gloire, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [les] donne ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne refuse pas le bien à ceux qui marchent dans l’intégrité.
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu est soleil et bouclier ; \q {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} donne la faveur et la gloire ; \q à ceux qui marchent sans reproche, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne refuse aucun bien.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu donne la lumière comme le soleil et protège comme un bouclier. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} montre de la bonté et donne l’honneur. \q Il ne refuse rien de bon à ceux qui vivent sans reproche.

sw.L: Kwa maana jua na ngao [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu; \q neema na heshima {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hutoa; \q hawanyimi mema wale waendao katika ukamilifu.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu ni jua na ngao; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hutoa neema na heshima; \q wale waendao bila lawama hawanyimi kitu chochote chema.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu hutoa nuru kama jua na hulinda kama ngao. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huonyesha wema na hutoa heshima. \q Hawanyimi kitu chochote chema watu wanaoishi bila lawama.

es.L: Porque sol y escudo [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios; \q favor y honra da {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; \q no niega el bien a los que andan en integridad.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios es sol y escudo; \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} da favor y honra; \q a los que andan sin tacha no les niega ningún bien.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios da luz como el sol y protege como un escudo. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} muestra bondad y da honra. \q No les niega nada bueno a los que viven sin culpa.

vi.L: Vì mặt trời và cái khiên [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời; \q ơn và vinh hiển {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không giữ lại điều tốt khỏi những người bước đi trong sự trọn vẹn.
vi.B: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời vừa là mặt trời vừa là cái khiên; \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban ơn và vinh dự; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng tiếc điều tốt lành nào với những người sống trọn vẹn.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời ban ánh sáng như mặt trời và bảo vệ như cái khiên. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tỏ lòng tốt và ban danh dự. \q Ngài không giữ lại điều tốt nào khỏi những người sống không có gì đáng trách.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님은 해와 방패이시니, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 은혜와 영광을 주시고, \q 흠 없이 걷는 사람들에게서 좋은 것을 거두지 않으신다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님은 해와 방패이시다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 은혜와 영광을 베푸시고, \q 흠 없이 사는 사람들에게 좋은 것을 아끼지 않으신다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님은 해처럼 빛을 주시고 방패처럼 지켜 주신다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 은혜를 베푸시고 영광을 주신다. \q 흠 없이 사는 사람들에게 좋은 것을 하나도 아끼지 않으신다.

pt.L: Pois sol e escudo [é] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus; \q favor e honra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dá; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não nega o bem aos que andam em integridade.
pt.B: Pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus é sol e escudo; \q {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} concede favor e honra; \q aos que andam de modo irrepreensível {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não recusa nenhum bem.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} Deus dá luz como o sol e protege como um escudo. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} mostra bondade e dá honra. \q Ele não deixa faltar nada de bom a quem vive sem culpa.

decisions.choice: a sun: the giver of light and life
decisions.reason: Only here is God called a sun. The sun gives light and warmth and makes things grow; the shield protects (3:4).

decisions.choice: a sun and a shield: the Hebrew text
alternatives: the LORD loves mercy and truth (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation has "for the LORD God loves mercy and truth" here. The Hebrew text has "sun and shield".

decisions.choice: favor and honor
decisions.reason: The first word (chen) is kindness shown freely; the second (kavod) is honor or glory, the weight and standing God gives.

decisions.choice: blamelessness: a whole and honest life
decisions.reason: The word (tamim) means complete, without fault (15:2; 18:24).

decisions.choice: gives light like the sun and protects like a shield
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m1).

decisions.choice: This verse speaks about the LORD in the plain written style with the honorific (-시-, 께서)
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks of God in the third person here, so Korean uses the voice the style guide (section 7a) gives to speech about God; verse 13 turns back to address him.

records.literal_gloss: YHWH of hosts, how blessed [is the] person [who] trusts in you!

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q how blessed [is the] {{gender:person|man}} [who] trusts in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q how blessed is anyone who trusts in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q life is truly good for anyone who trusts in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q {{gender:heureuse la personne|heureux l’homme}} [qui] se confie en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} !
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q heureux celui qui se confie en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} !
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q celui qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} fait confiance est vraiment heureux !

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q heri mtu akutegemeaye!
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q heri kila mtu anayekutumainia!
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa kila mtu anayekutumainia!

es.L: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, \q ¡{{gender:dichosa la persona|dichoso el hombre}} que confía en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}!
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q ¡qué dichoso es todo el que confía en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}!
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q ¡qué buena es la vida de todo el que confía en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}!

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q phước thay người tin cậy nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}!
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q phước hạnh thay người nào tin cậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}!
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q thật hạnh phúc cho người nào tin cậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}!

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, \q 주님을 신뢰하는 사람은 얼마나 복된지요!
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, \q 주님을 신뢰하는 사람은 누구나 얼마나 복됩니까!
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, \q 주님을 믿고 의지하는 사람은 누구나 참으로 행복합니다!

pt.L: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, \q bem-aventurado [é] {{gender:o ser humano|o homem}} [que] confia em {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}!
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, \q como é feliz todo aquele que confia em {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}!
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, \q feliz de verdade é quem confia em {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}!

decisions.choice: how blessed: truly happy
decisions.reason: As in verses 5 and 6, the third "how blessed" of the psalm.

decisions.choice: the person: anyone
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) means a human being, man or woman.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: The title (YHWH tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.
